env_103_sft.environment_introduction: A document management system is a centralized environment for storing, organizing, and retrieving electronic documents or reports. It maintains state through unique identifiers, access controls, versioning, and metadata associated with each document. Such systems support operations like creation, retrieval, update, and deletion of documents in a structured and auditable manner.

state_space_definition.attributes: document_id, title, content, creation_date, last_modified_date, version, status, owner_id, access_permission
state_space_definition.description: Represents a stored document (e.g., report) in the system, uniquely identified by document_id and associated with metadata and access rules.

state_space_definition.attributes: _id, name, role, departmen
state_space_definition.description: Represents individuals interacting with the system; used for access control and ownership tracking.

state_space_definition.attributes: document_id, user_id, permissions (read, write, delete)
state_space_definition.description: fines which users have what level of access to each document.

state_space_definition.attributes: version_id, document_id, version_number, content_snapshot, timestamp, modified_by
state_space_definition.description: Tracks historical versions of a document to support versioning.

constraints_rules: Only documents with status = "active" can be retrieved.
A user must have 'read' permission on a document to retrieve it.
Each document must have a unique document_id.
The system maintains at least one version (current) for each document.
Access permissions are enforced during retrieval operations.

operation_list.operation_description: Retrieve a document's metadata and content by document_id, only if status is "active" and the requester has read permission.
List all documents in the system with status "active".
Return the current status (e.g., active, archived, deleted) of a document.
Retrieve the list of users and their access permissions (read, write, delete) for a given document.
Determine whether a specific user has a given permission (e.g., read) on a document.
Retrieve the version history of a document, including version numbers, timestamps, and modifiers.
Retrieve the current (latest) version metadata and snapshot of a document.
Retrieve only the content of a document if it is active and accessible.
Search for documents by title with case-insensitive matching.
Create a new document with initial content and metadata, assign a unique document_id, and create its first version.
Modify a document’s content or metadata, increment version number, and create a new version snapshot.
Mark a document as "deleted" (soft delete) or remove it, depending on policy; access no longer allowed.
Restore a deleted or archived document to "active" status.
Define or update access permissions for a user on a specific document (e.g., grant read/write).
Remove a user’s access permissions to a document.
Change document status to "archived", making it non-retrievable in normal queries.
Restore a document to a previous version by creating a new version based on a past snapshot.
Set a document’s status to "active" from draft or archived state, enabling retrieval.

from typing import Dict, List, Optional
from datetime import datetime



class DocumentInfo(TypedDict):
    document_id: str
    title: str
    content: str
    creation_date: str
    last_modified_date: str
    version: int
    status: str
    owner_id: str
    access_permission: str  # Could be a string like "read,write" or we use AccessControlEntry instead

class UserInfo(TypedDict):
    _id: str
    name: str
    role: str
    department: str

class AccessControlEntryInfo(TypedDict):
    document_id: str
    user_id: str
    permissions: List[str]  # e.g., ["read"], ["read", "write"], etc.

class DocumentVersionInfo(TypedDict):
    version_id: str
    document_id: str
    version_number: int
    content_snapshot: str
    timestamp: str
    modified_by: str


class DocumentManagementSystem:
    def __init__(self):
        """
        A document management system for managing electronic documents with access control and versioning.
        """

        # Documents: {document_id: DocumentInfo}
        self.documents: Dict[str, DocumentInfo] = {}

        # Users: {user_id: UserInfo}
        self.users: Dict[str, UserInfo] = {}

        # Access control: {document_id: {user_id: permissions_list}}
        self.access_control: Dict[str, Dict[str, List[str]]] = {}

        # Document versions: {version_id: DocumentVersionInfo}
        self.versions: Dict[str, DocumentVersionInfo] = {}

        # Constraints reminder:
        # - Only documents with status = "active" can be retrieved
        # - A user must have 'read' permission on a document to retrieve it
        # - Each document must have a unique document_id
        # - The system maintains at least one version (current) for each document
        # - Access permissions are enforced during retrieval operations

function.name: get_document_by_id
function.description:
Retrieve a document's metadata and content by document_id, only if the document status is "active"
and the requesting user has 'read' permission.

Args:
    document_id (str): The unique ID of the document to retrieve.
    user_id (str): The ID of the user attempting to access the document.

Returns:
    dict: {
        "success": True,
        "data": DocumentInfo
    }
    or
    {
        "success": False,
        "error": str  # Explanation of why access was denied or failed
    }

Constraints:
    - Only documents with status = "active" can be retrieved.
    - A user must have 'read' permission on the document to retrieve it.
    - Access permissions are enforced during retrieval.

function.name: list_active_documents
function.description:
List all documents in the system with status "active".

Returns:
    dict: {
        "success": True,
        "data": List[DocumentInfo]  # List of documents where status == "active"
    }
    or, in case of no matches, an empty list is returned under "data".

Constraints:
    - Only documents with status = "active" are included.
    - Each document in the result must have a unique document_id (enforced by system invariant).

function.name: check_document_status
get_document_permissions
check_user_access
function.description:
Determine whether a specific user has a given permission (e.g., 'read') on a document.

Args:
    user_id (str): The ID of the user.
    document_id (str): The ID of the document.
    permission (str): The permission to check (e.g., 'read', 'write', 'delete').

Returns:
    dict: {
        "success": bool,
        "data": bool  # True if user has the permission, False otherwise
    }
    or
    {
        "success": False,
        "error": str  # Description of validation or lookup error
    }

Constraints:
    - The user must exist in the system.
    - The document must exist in the system.
    - Access is determined by entries in the access control list.

function.name: get_document_version_history
function.description:
Retrieve the version history of a document, including version numbers, timestamps, and modifiers.

Args:
    document_id (str): The unique identifier of the document.
    user_id (str): The ID of the user requesting the version history (for access control).

Returns:
    dict: {
        "success": bool,
        "data": List[DocumentVersionInfo]  # Sorted by version_number ascending
    }
    or
    {
        "success": False,
        "error": str  # Reason for failure: document not found, not active, access denied, etc.
    }

Constraints:
    - Only documents with status = "active" can be retrieved.
    - A user must have 'read' permission on the document to retrieve its version history.
    - The system maintains at least one version for each document (guaranteed).

function.name: get_document_current_version
function.description:
Retrieve the current (latest) version of a document, including metadata and content snapshot.

Args:
    document_id (str): The unique identifier of the document.

Returns:
    dict: {
        "success": bool,
        "data": DocumentVersionInfo  # If successful
    }
    or
    {
        "success": False,
        "error": str  # Description of the error
    }

Constraints:
    - The document must exist and have status "active".
    - The system must maintain at least one version per document (if none, it's an error).

function.name: get_document_content
function.description:
Retrieve the content of a document if it is active and the user has read permission.

Args:
    document_id (str): The unique identifier of the document.
    user_id (str): The ID of the user requesting access.

Returns:
    dict: {
        "success": True,
        "data": str  # The content of the document
    }
    or
    {
        "success": False,
        "error": str  # Explanation of why access was denied
    }

Constraints:
    - Only documents with status = "active" can be retrieved.
    - A user must have 'read' permission on the document to retrieve it.
    - Access permissions are enforced during retrieval.

function.name: search_documents_by_title
function.description:
Search for documents by title using case-insensitive substring matching.
Only documents with status "active" are included in the search results.

Args:
    title_query (str): The substring to search for in document titles.

Returns:
    dict: {
        "success": True,
        "data": List[DocumentInfo]  # List of matching active documents (may be empty)
    }
    or
    {
        "success": False,
        "error": str  # Only if an unexpected issue occurs (not expected here)
    }

Constraints:
    - Only documents with status == "active" are returned.
    - Case-insensitive matching is performed on the title.
    - No access control check is performed due to absence of user_id in parameters.

function.name: create_document
function.description:
Create a new document with initial metadata and version.

Args:
    title (str): The title of the document.
    content (str): The initial content of the document.
    owner_id (str): The ID of the user who will own the document.
    permissions (List[str], optional): List of initial permissions for the owner.
        Defaults to ["read", "write"].

Returns:
    dict: {
        "success": True,
        "message": "Document created successfully with ID: <document_id>"
    }
    or
    {
        "success": False,
        "error": str  # Description of the error
    }

Constraints:
    - owner_id must correspond to an existing user.
    - document_id must be unique.
    - A document is created with status "active".
    - The first version is recorded in version history.
    - Owner is granted read (and optionally write) access.

function.name: update_document
function.description:
Update a document's title or content, increment its version, and create a new version snapshot.

Args:
    document_id (str): The ID of the document to update.
    user_id (str): The ID of the user making the update.
    title (str, optional): New title for the document.
    content (str, optional): New content for the document.

Returns:
    dict: {
        "success": bool,
        "message": str  # On success: description of update and new version
    }
    or
    {
        "success": False,
        "error": str  # Reason for failure
    }

Constraints:
    - Document must exist and have status "active".
    - User must have "write" permission on the document.
    - At least one of title or content must be provided.
    - A new version entry is created with the updated content or current content.

function.name: delete_document
function.description:
Mark a document as deleted (soft delete) so it can no longer be accessed.
The document status is set to 'deleted'. Access is revoked and it will not appear in active queries.

Args:
    document_id (str): The unique identifier of the document to delete.
    user_id (str): The ID of the user attempting the deletion (must have delete or write permission).

Returns:
    dict: {
        "success": True,
        "message": "Document deleted successfully."
    }
    or
    {
        "success": False,
        "error": str  # e.g., "Document not found", "User does not have permission", etc.
    }

Constraints:
    - The user must have 'delete' or appropriate permission (e.g., write and ownership) to delete.
    - Only active documents can be deleted (not already deleted).
    - Document ID must exist.
    - After deletion, document is no longer retrievable (status becomes 'deleted').

function.name: restore_document
function.description:
Restore a document to "active" status if it exists and has at least one version.

Args:
    document_id (str): The unique identifier of the document to restore.

Returns:
    dict: {
        "success": bool,
        "message": str  # On success
    } or {
        "success": False,
        "error": str  # Reason for failure
    }

Constraints:
    - The document must exist.
    - The document must have at least one version (in self.versions) linked to it.
    - After restore, status becomes "active".

function.name: set_document_permissions
function.description:
Define or update access permissions for a user on a specific document.

Args:
    document_id (str): The unique identifier of the document.
    user_id (str): The unique identifier of the user.
    permissions (List[str]): List of permissions to grant. Valid values: 'read', 'write', 'delete'.

Returns:
    dict: {
        "success": bool,
        "message": str  # On success
    }
    or
    {
        "success": bool,
        "error": str  # On failure
    }

Constraints:
    - The document must exist.
    - The user must exist.
    - Permissions must be a subset of ['read', 'write', 'delete'].
    - Setting permissions does not require the document to be active.

Note:
    This operation overwrites existing permissions for the user on the document.

function.name: revoke_user_access
function.description:
Remove a user’s access permissions to a specific document.

Args:
    document_id (str): The unique identifier of the document.
    user_id (str): The unique identifier of the user whose access is to be revoked.

Returns:
    dict: {
        "success": True,
        "message": str  # Describes the revocation result
    }
    or
    {
        "success": False,
        "error": str  # Reason for failure (e.g. document or user not found)
    }

Constraints:
    - The document must exist in the system.
    - The user must exist in the system.
    - After revocation, the user will no longer have any permissions on the document.
    - Revoking non-granted access is allowed and treated as success.

function.name: archive_document
function.description:
Change the status of a document to 'archived', making it non-retrievable in normal queries.

Args:
    document_id (str): The unique identifier of the document to archive.

Returns:
    dict: {
        "success": True,
        "message": "Document archived successfully"
    }
    or
    {
        "success": False,
        "error": "Document not found"
    }

Constraints:
    - The document must exist in the system.
    - After archiving, the document will no longer be retrievable by operations that require status = 'active'.
    - This operation does not require explicit permission checks as per current constraints (only retrieval enforces access).

function.name: revert_to_version
function.description:
Restore a document to a previous version by creating a new version based on a past snapshot.

Args:
    document_id (str): The ID of the document to revert.
    version_id (str): The ID of the version to revert to.
    user_id (str): The ID of the user performing the revert.

Returns:
    dict: {
        "success": bool,
        "message": str  # On success: description of revert
    }
    or
    {
        "success": False,
        "error": str  # Reason for failure
    }

Constraints:
    - Document must exist and have status "active".
    - The version must exist and belong to the document.
    - User must have "write" permission on the document.
    - A new version entry is created; document version and content are updated.

function.name: publish_document
function.description:
Set a document's status to "active", enabling it to be retrieved by authorized users.

Args:
    document_id (str): The unique identifier of the document to publish.

Returns:
    dict: {
        "success": bool,
        "message": str  # On success
    }
    or
    {
        "success": False,
        "error": str  # On failure (e.g., document not found)
    }

Constraints:
    - The document must exist.
    - After publishing, the document becomes retrievable (if status == "active").
    - This operation does not verify user permissions; assumes caller has appropriate rights.

env_106_sft.environment_introduction: A machine learning experiment management system is a stateful environment that tracks datasets, model configurations, training progress, and evaluation results across time. It maintains persistent state such as feature sets, trained models, hyperparameters, and performance logs. This environment supports iterative model development by enabling controlled training, feature selection, and scheduled evaluation, commonly used in data science workflows.

state_space_definition.attributes: dataset_id, name, file_path, schema, version, created_a
state_space_definition.description: Represents a data source used for training and evaluation, including its location and structure.

state_space_definition.attributes: config_id, model_type, hyperparameters, feature_set, description
state_space_definition.description: Stores the specification of a model, including algorithm (e.g., RandomForest, regression), hyperparameters (e.g., learning rate, iterations), and selected features.

state_space_definition.attributes: xperiment_id, dataset_id, config_id, status, start_time, end_time, current_iteration
state_space_definition.description: Represents a single machine learning experiment, tracking its execution state and associated configurations.

state_space_definition.attributes: lection_id, experiment_id, method, importance_scores, selected_features, threshold
state_space_definition.description: Captures the outcome of a feature selection step, including which features were retained based on a metric (e.g., gain threshold).

state_space_definition.attributes: valuation_id, experiment_id, iteration, metrics (e.g., RMSE, MAE), evaluated_a
state_space_definition.description: Records performance metrics at specific points during training, enabling progress tracking.

constraints_rules: Feature selection must be completed before model training begins.
Evaluation must occur at specified intervals (e.g., midway and every 10 days) based on training duration or iteration count.
Model training cannot start if the dataset referenced by file_path does not exist or is invalid.
Hyperparameters must be validated against model type constraints (e.g., learning rate only applicable for iterative models).
An experiment's status must reflect its current phase (e.g., "pending", "running", "completed", "failed").

Find a dataset using its file_path (e.g., 'rental_prices.csv') to verify existence and retrieve its ID and schema.
Retrieve all registered datasets in the system for exploration or audit.
Retrieve a model configuration (model_type, hyperparameters, feature_set) by config_id.
List all configurations filtered by model type (e.g., RandomForest, LinearRegression).
Query the current status (pending, running, completed, failed) of an experiment.
Retrieve full details of an experiment, including dataset, config, and timing.
Retrieve all experiments filtered by status (e.g., running, completed).
Retrieve the result of feature selection (selected_features, importance_scores) for a given experiment.
Retrieve all evaluation metrics logged for a specific experiment or iteration.
Verify whether the dataset file_path points to an existing and accessible file.
Retrieve the current training iteration of a running experiment for scheduling evaluations.
Define a new model configuration with model_type, hyperparameters, and feature_set, with validation against model constraints (e.g., learning rate only for iterative models).
Execute feature selection (e.g., SHAP, gain-based) on a dataset using a specified model configuration and store the selected features and importance scores.
Initialize a new experiment with a dataset and model configuration, set status to "running", and record start time.
Change the status of an experiment (e.g., from "running" to "completed" or "failed") based on execution outcome.
Record evaluation metrics (e.g., RMSE, MAE) at a specific iteration and timestamp during training.
Temporarily halt a running experiment and update status to "paused".
Resume a paused experiment and continue training from the last iteration.
Terminate an experiment and set status to "cancelled".
Add a new dataset to the system with metadata (name, file_path, schema, version).
Modify an existing model configuration (e.g., adjust hyperparameters) with proper validation.
Force an evaluation at the midway point of training iterations if not already scheduled.
Set up automatic evaluation logging every N days or iterations (e.g., every 10 days).

        self,
        config_id: str,

        hyperparameters: dict,
        feature_set: List[str],
        description: str = ""
    ) -> dict:
        """
        Define a new model configuration with model type, hyperparameters, and feature set.
        Performs validation to ensure hyperparameters are compatible with the model type.

        Args:
            config_id (str): Unique identifier for the model configuration.
            model_type (str): Type of model (e.g., 'RandomForest', 'LinearRegression').
            hyperparameters (dict): Key-value pairs of model hyperparameters.
            feature_set (List[str]): List of feature names used by the model.
            description (str): Optional description of the configuration.

        Returns:
            dict: {
                "success": bool,
                "message": str  # On success
            } or {
                "success": False,
                "error": str  # Reason for failure
            }

        Constraints:
            - config_id must be unique.
            - hyperparameters must be valid for the model type (e.g., 'learning_rate' only for iterative models).
            - feature_set must be a list of strings.
            - Model types that are iterative (e.g., 'NeuralNetwork', 'GradientBoosting') may accept 'learning_rate'.
            - Non-iterative models (e.g., 'RandomForest', 'LinearRegression') must not have 'learning_rate'.
        """
        # Validate config_id
        if not isinstance(config_id, str) or not config_id.strip():
            return {"success": False, "error": "config_id must be a non-empty string"}
        config_id = config_id.strip()

        if config_id in self.model_configurations:
            return {"success": False, "error": f"Model configuration with id '{config_id}' already exists"}

        # Validate model_type
        if not isinstance(model_type, str) or not model_type.strip():
            return {"success": False, "error": "model_type must be a non-empty string"}
        model_type = model_type.strip()

        # Validate hyperparameters
        if not isinstance(hyperparameters, dict):
            return {"success": False, "error": "hyperparameters must be a dictionary"}

        # Define which models are considered iterative and can have 'learning_rate'
        iterative_models = {"NeuralNetwork", "GradientBoosting", "XGBoost", "SGD", "AdaBoost"}
        if model_type in iterative_models:
            # Allow 'learning_rate'
            pass
        else:
            # For non-iterative models, disallow 'learning_rate'
            if "learning_rate" in hyperparameters:
                return {
                    "success": False,
                    "error": f"Model type '{model_type}' does not support 'learning_rate' hyperparameter"
                }

        # Validate feature_set
        if not isinstance(feature_set, list):
            return {"success": False, "error": "feature_set must be a list of strings"}
        if not all(isinstance(f, str) for f in feature_set):
            return {"success": False, "error": "All features in feature_set must be strings"}

        # Validate description
        if not isinstance(description, str):
            return {"success": False, "error": "description must be a string"}
        description = description.strip()

        # Create new configuration
        new_config: ModelConfigurationInfo = {
            "config_id": config_id,
            "model_type": model_type,
            "hyperparameters": hyperparameters,
            "feature_set": feature_set,
            "description": description
        }

        self.model_configurations[config_id] = new_config

    - Method must be a non-empty string.", "source_code": "    def run_feature_selection(self, experiment_id: str, method: str, threshold: float) -> dict:
        """
        Execute feature selection on the dataset associated with the given experiment
        using its model configuration, and store the importance scores and selected features.

        Args:
            experiment_id (str): Unique identifier for the experiment.
            method (str): Feature selection method (e.g., 'SHAP', 'Permutation Importance', 'Gain-based').
            threshold (float): Minimum importance score for a feature to be selected.

        Returns:
            dict: {
                "success": bool,
                "message": str  # On success: description of result
            }
            or {
                "success": False,
                "error": str  # Reason for failure
            }

        Constraints:
            - Feature selection must occur before training begins (experiment status must be 'pending').
            - Dataset must exist and be valid (file_path accessible).
            - Model configuration must exist and have a non-empty feature_set.
            - Threshold must be positive.
            - Method must be a non-empty string.
        """
        # Validate inputs
        if not isinstance(experiment_id, str) or not experiment_id:
            return {"success": False, "error": "Invalid experiment_id: must be a non-empty string"}
        if not isinstance(method, str) or not method:
            return {"success": False, "error": "Invalid method: must be a non-empty string"}
        if not isinstance(threshold, (float, int)) or threshold <= 0:
            return {"success": False, "error": "Invalid threshold: must be a positive number"}

        # Check if experiment exists
        if experiment_id not in self.experiments:
            return {"success": False, "error": f"Experiment with ID '{experiment_id}' not found"}

        experiment = self.experiments[experiment_id]

        # Check experiment status: must be 'pending' (before training)
        if experiment["status"] != "pending":
            return {
                "success": False,
                "error": f"Feature selection can only be run in 'pending' status, but current status is '{experiment['status']}'"
            }

        # Check dataset exists and is valid
        dataset_id = experiment["dataset_id"]
        if dataset_id not in self.datasets:
            return {"success": False, "error": f"Dataset with ID '{dataset_id}' not found"}

        dataset = self.datasets[dataset_id]
        # Simulate file validity check
        try:
            # In real system, check file_path exists and is readable
            if not dataset["file_path"]:
                return {"success": False, "error": "Dataset file_path is missing"}
            # For simulation, we assume file_path is valid if non-empty
        except Exception:
            return {"success": False, "error": "Dataset file_path is invalid or inaccessible"}

        # Get model configuration
        config_id = experiment["config_id"]
        if config_id not in self.model_configurations:
            return {"success": False, "error": f"Model configuration with ID '{config_id}' not found"}

        config = self.model_configurations[config_id]
        feature_set = config["feature_set"]
        if not feature_set:
            return {"success": False, "error": "Model configuration has no feature set defined"}

        # Simulate importance scoring (in real system, this would be computed)
        # Here we assign mock scores (e.g., based on feature name hash for determinism)
        importance_scores = {}
        for feature in feature_set:
            # Mock importance score: deterministic based on feature name
            score = abs(hash(feature)) % 100 / 100.0  # Random-like float between 0 and 1
            importance_scores[feature] = round(score, 4)

        # Select features above threshold
        selected_features = [feat for feat, score in importance_scores.items() if score >= threshold]

        # Generate selection_id
        selection_id = f"{experiment_id}_fs_{method.lower().replace(' ', '_')}"

        # Store result
        feature_selection_result: FeatureSelectionResultInfo = {
            "selection_id": selection_id,
            "experiment_id": experiment_id,
            "method": method,
            "importance_scores": importance_scores,
            "selected_features": selected_features,
            "threshold": threshold
        }

        self.feature_selection_results[selection_id] = feature_selection_result

        return {
            "success": True,
            "message": f"Feature selection completed using '{method}' method for experiment '{experiment_id}'. "
                       f"{len(selected_features)} features selected out of {len(feature_set)} using threshold {threshold}."
        }"}, "start_experiment": {"signature": {"parameters": [{"name": "experiment_id", "type": "str", "default": null, "kind": "positional-or-keyword"}], "return": "dict"}, "doc": "Initialize and start a pending experiment by setting its status to "running" and recording the start time.

        """
        Initialize and start a pending experiment by setting its status to "running" and recording the start time.
    
        Args:
            experiment_id (str): The ID of the experiment to start.

        Returns:
            dict: {
                "success": True,
                "message": "Experiment started successfully"
            }
            or
            {
                "success": False,
                "error": str  # Description of failure reason
            }

        Constraints:
            - Experiment must exist and be in "pending" status.
            - Dataset referenced by experiment must exist and have a valid file_path.
            - Model configuration must exist.
            - Feature selection must have been completed for the experiment.
        """
        # Get experiment
        experiment = self.experiments.get(experiment_id)
        if not experiment:
            return { "success": False, "error": "Experiment does not exist" }

        if experiment["status"] != "pending":
            return { "success": False, "error": f"Experiment cannot be started; current status is '{experiment['status']}'" }

        # Check dataset exists and is valid
        dataset_id = experiment["dataset_id"]
        dataset = self.datasets.get(dataset_id)
        if not dataset:
            return { "success": False, "error": "Dataset referenced by experiment does not exist" }
        if not dataset["file_path"]:
            return { "success": False, "error": "Dataset file_path is invalid or missing" }

        # Check model configuration exists
        config_id = experiment["config_id"]
        if config_id not in self.model_configurations:
            return { "success": False, "error": "Model configuration referenced by experiment does not exist" }

        # Check feature selection has been completed
        has_feature_selection = any(
            result["experiment_id"] == experiment_id
            for result in self.feature_selection_results.values()
        )
        if not has_feature_selection:
            return { "success": False, "error": "Feature selection must be completed before starting training" }

        # Update experiment state
        experiment["status"] = "running"
        experiment["start_time"] = datetime.now().isoformat()
        if experiment["current_iteration"] is None:
            experiment["current_iteration"] = 0

        return { "success": True, "message": "Experiment started successfully" }"}, "update_experiment_status": {"signature": {"parameters": [{"name": "experiment_id", "type": "str", "default": null, "kind": "positional-or-keyword"}, {"name": "new_status", "type": "str", "default": null, "kind": "positional-or-keyword"}], "return": "dict"}, "doc": "Change the status of an experiment based on execution outcome.

        """
        Add a new dataset to the system with metadata.

        Args:
            name (str): Name of the dataset.
            file_path (str): Path to the dataset file.
            schema (dict): Structure of the dataset (e.g., column types).
            version (str): Version string of the dataset.

        Returns:
            dict: {
                "success": bool,
                "message": str,
                "dataset_id": str  # Only included if successful
            }
            or
            {
                "success": False,
                "error": str  # Description of the validation or registration failure
            }

        Constraints:
            - All input fields must be valid and non-empty.
            - schema must be a dictionary.
            - file_path should be a non-empty string.
            - A unique dataset_id is generated upon registration.

        Note:
            - File existence is not checked at registration time (checked during training).
        """
        # Validate inputs
        if not name or not isinstance(name, str):
            return {"success": False, "error": "Name must be a non-empty string"}
        if not file_path or not isinstance(file_path, str):
            return {"success": False, "error": "File path must be a non-empty string"}
        if not isinstance(schema, dict) or len(schema) == 0:
            return {"success": False, "error": "Schema must be a non-empty dictionary"}
        if not version or not isinstance(version, str):
            return {"success": False, "error": "Version must be a non-empty string"}

        # Generate dataset_id
        dataset_id = f"dataset_{len(self.datasets) + 1}"

        # Ensure no ID collision (though unlikely with this scheme)
        while dataset_id in self.datasets:
            dataset_id = f"{dataset_id}_1"

        # Create dataset entry
        created_at = datetime.utcnow().isoformat() + "Z"

        self.datasets[dataset_id] = {
            "dataset_id": dataset_id,
            "name": name,
            "file_path": file_path,
            "schema": schema,
            "version": version,
            "created_at": created_at
        }

        return {
            "success": True,
            "message": "Dataset registered successfully",
            "dataset_id": dataset_id
        }"}, "update_model_configuration": {"signature": {"parameters": [{"name": "config_id", "type": "str", "default": null, "kind": "positional-or-keyword"}, {"name": "updates", "type": "dict", "default": null, "kind": "positional-or-keyword"}], "return": "dict"}, "doc": "Modify an existing model configuration with proper validation of hyperparameters and other fields.

        """
        Modify an existing model configuration with proper validation of hyperparameters and other fields.

        Args:
            config_id (str): The ID of the model configuration to update.
            updates (dict): A dictionary containing fields to update. Supported keys:
                - hyperparameters (dict): Key-value pairs for model hyperparameters.
                - feature_set (List[str]): List of feature names to use.
                - description (str): Description of the configuration.

        Returns:
            dict: {
                "success": bool,
                "message": str  # On success
            }
            or
            {
                "success": False,
                "error": str  # Reason for failure
            }

        Constraints:
            - The config_id must exist.
            - Hyperparameters must be valid for the model type (e.g., learning_rate only for iterative models).
            - feature_set must be a list of strings if provided.
        """
        if config_id not in self.model_configurations:
            return { "success": False, "error": f"Model configuration with ID '{config_id}' does not exist." }

        config = self.model_configurations[config_id]
        model_type = config["model_type"]

        # Validate hyperparameters if present in updates
        if "hyperparameters" in updates:
            hyperparams = updates["hyperparameters"]
            if not isinstance(hyperparams, dict):
                return { "success": False, "error": "Hyperparameters must be a dictionary." }

            # Example validation rules based on model type
            iterative_models = ["GradientBoosting", "NeuralNetwork", "XGBoost", "AdaBoost"]
            if model_type in iterative_models:
                lr = hyperparams.get("learning_rate")
                if lr is not None:
                    if not isinstance(lr, (float, int)) or lr <= 0:
                        return { "success": False, "error": "learning_rate must be a positive number for iterative models." }
            else:
                # Check for disallowed hyperparameters in non-iterative models
                if "learning_rate" in hyperparams:
                    return { "success": False, "error": "learning_rate is not a valid hyperparameter for this model type." }

            # Additional example: n_estimators should be positive integer
            n_est = hyperparams.get("n_estimators")
            if n_est is not None and (not isinstance(n_est, int) or n_est <= 0):
                return { "success": False, "error": "n_estimators must be a positive integer." }

            # Merge valid hyperparameters
            config["hyperparameters"].update(hyperparams)

        # Validate and update feature_set
        if "feature_set" in updates:
            feature_set = updates["feature_set"]
            if not isinstance(feature_set, list) or not all(isinstance(f, str) for f in feature_set):
                return { "success": False, "error": "feature_set must be a list of strings." }
            config["feature_set"] = feature_set

        # Update description
        if "description" in updates:
            desc = updates["description"]
            if not isinstance(desc, str):
                return { "success": False, "error": "description must be a string." }
            config["description"] = desc

        # Save back to the configurations
        self.model_configurations[config_id] = config

        return { "success": True, "message": "Model configuration updated successfully." }"}, "trigger_midway_evaluation": {"signature": {"parameters": [{"name": "experiment_id", "type": "str", "default": null, "kind": "positional-or-keyword"}], "return": "dict"}, "doc": "Force an evaluation at the midway point of training iterations for the given experiment if not already present.

Args:
    experiment_id (str): The ID of the experiment.

Returns:
    dict: {
        "success": True,
        "message": "Midway evaluation triggered for experiment <id> at iteration <midway_iter>."
    }
    or
    {
        "success": False,
        "error": str  # Description of the error
    }

Constraints:
    - Experiment must exist and not be 'failed' or 'completed'
    - Midway point is integer division of max observed iteration, or possibly from current_iteration if that's the best available
    - If evaluation already present for midway point, do not duplicate", "source_code": "    def trigger_midway_evaluation(self, experiment_id: str) -> dict:
        """
        Force an evaluation at the midway point of training iterations for the given experiment if not already present.

        Args:
            experiment_id (str): The ID of the experiment.

        Returns:
            dict: {
                "success": True,
                "message": "Midway evaluation triggered for experiment <id> at iteration <midway_iter>."
            }
            or
            {
                "success": False,
                "error": str  # Description of the error
            }

        Constraints:
            - Experiment must exist and not be 'failed' or 'completed'
            - Midway point is integer division of max observed iteration, or possibly from current_iteration if that's the best available
            - If evaluation already present for midway point, do not duplicate
        """
        # Step 1: Check experiment exists
        exp = self.experiments.get(experiment_id)
        if not exp:
            return { "success": False, "error": f"Experiment '{experiment_id}' not found." }

        if exp["status"] in ["failed", "completed"]:
            return { "success": False, "error": f"Cannot trigger evaluation for experiment status: {exp['status']}" }

        # Step 2: Find max iteration from evaluation_results for this experiment
        experiment_evals = [
            eval_info for eval_info in self.evaluation_results.values()
            if eval_info["experiment_id"] == experiment_id
        ]
        # Get highest iteration; fallback to experiment's current_iteration if no evaluations yet
        iterations = [e["iteration"] for e in experiment_evals]
        current_max_iter = max(iterations) if iterations else exp.get("current_iteration", None)

        if current_max_iter is None or current_max_iter <= 1:
            return { "success": False, "error": "Insufficient training iterations to determine midway point." }

        midway_iter = current_max_iter // 2

        # Step 3: Check if evaluation already scheduled at midway iteration
        already_exists = any(
            e["iteration"] == midway_iter for e in experiment_evals
        )
        if already_exists:
            return { "success": True, "message": f"Midway evaluation already triggered for experiment {experiment_id} at iteration {midway_iter}." }

        # Step 4: Generate evaluation_id (e.g., combine experiment_id and midway_iter)
        evaluation_id = f"{experiment_id}_midway_{midway_iter}"

        # Step 5: Create evaluation result with default metrics (empty) and current timestamp
        evaluated_at = datetime.utcnow().isoformat()
        eval_info = {
            "evaluation_id": evaluation_id,
            "experiment_id": experiment_id,
            "iteration": midway_iter,
            "metrics": {},  # Default empty metrics, to be filled in by actual evaluation
            "evaluated_at": evaluated_at
        }
        self.evaluation_results[evaluation_id] = eval_info

        return {
            "success": True,
            "message": f"Midway evaluation triggered for experiment {experiment_id} at iteration {midway_iter}."
        }"}, "schedule_periodic_evaluation": {"signature": {"parameters": [{"name": "experiment_id", "type": "str", "default": null, "kind": "positional-or-keyword"}, {"name": "interval_type", "type": "str", "default": null, "kind": "positional-or-keyword"}, {"name": "interval_value", "type": "int", "default": null, "kind": "positional-or-keyword"}], "return": "dict"}, "doc": "Set up automatic evaluation logging at regular intervals (by days or iterations) for a given experiment.

Args:
    experiment_id (str): Unique identifier of the experiment to schedule.
    interval_type (str): The basis for scheduling — must be 'days' or 'iterations'.
    interval_value (int): Positive integer indicating the frequency of evaluation.

Returns:
    dict: {
        "success": True,
        "message": str  # Confirmation of schedule
    }
    or
    {
        "success": False,
        "error": str  # Reason for failure
    }

Constraints:
    - The experiment must exist and not be in a terminal state.
    - interval_type must be 'days' or 'iterations'.
    - interval_value must be a positive integer.
    - Evaluation scheduling respects system constraints (e.g., evaluation rules).", "source_code": "    def schedule_periodic_evaluation(self, experiment_id: str, interval_type: str, interval_value: int) -> dict:
        """
        Set up automatic evaluation logging at regular intervals (by days or iterations) for a given experiment.

        Args:
            experiment_id (str): Unique identifier of the experiment to schedule.
            interval_type (str): The basis for scheduling — must be 'days' or 'iterations'.
            interval_value (int): Positive integer indicating the frequency of evaluation.

        Returns:
            dict: {
                "success": True,
                "message": str  # Confirmation of schedule
            }
            or
            {
                "success": False,
                "error": str  # Reason for failure
            }

        Constraints:
            - The experiment must exist and not be in a terminal state.
            - interval_type must be 'days' or 'iterations'.
            - interval_value must be a positive integer.
            - Evaluation scheduling respects system constraints (e.g., evaluation rules).
        """
        # Validate interval_type
        if interval_type not in ['days', 'iterations']:
            return {
                "success": False,
                "error": "interval_type must be 'days' or 'iterations'"
            }

        if not isinstance(interval_value, int) or interval_value <= 0:
            return {
                "success": False,
                "error": "interval_value must be a positive integer"
            }

        # Check if experiment exists
        if experiment_id not in self.experiments:
            return {
                "success": False,
                "error": f"Experiment with ID '{experiment_id}' not found"
            }

        experiment = self.experiments[experiment_id]

        # Check if experiment is in a terminal state
        if experiment["status"] in ["completed", "failed", "cancelled"]:
            return {
                "success": False,
                "error": f"Cannot schedule evaluation: experiment is in '{experiment['status']}' state"
            }

        # Initialize scheduled_evaluations if not present (lazy initialization)
        if not hasattr(self, 'scheduled_evaluations'):
            self.scheduled_evaluations = {}

        # Store the schedule (overwrite if already exists)
        self.scheduled_evaluations[experiment_id] = {
            "interval_type": interval_type,
            "interval_value": interval_value
        }

        return {
            "success": True,
            "message": f"Periodic evaluation scheduled every {interval_value} {interval_type} for experiment '{experiment_id}'."
        }"}}

from typing import Dict, List, Tuple, TypedDict



class BusinessInfo(TypedDict):
    business_id: str
    name: str
    address: str
    city: str
    latitude: float
    longitude: float
    category: str
    phone: str
    website: str

class ReviewInfo(TypedDict):
    review_id: str
    business_id: str
    user_id: str
    rating: float
    text: str
    timestamp: str  # ISO format or Unix timestamp
    helpful_count: int

class UserInfo(TypedDict):
    user_id: str
    username: str
    join_date: str  # e.g., ISO format
    review_count: int
    reputation_score: int

class LocationInfo(TypedDict):
    city: str
    neighborhood: str
    coordinates_bounds: Tuple[Tuple[float, float], Tuple[float, float]]  # ((lat_min, lon_min), (lat_max, lon_max))

class OnlineLocalBusinessReviewPlatform:
    def __init__(self):
        """
        The environment for an online local business review platform.
        """

        # Businesses: {business_id: BusinessInfo}
        self.businesses: Dict[str, BusinessInfo] = {}

        # Reviews: {review_id: ReviewInfo}
        self.reviews: Dict[str, ReviewInfo] = {}

        # Users: {user_id: UserInfo}
        self.users: Dict[str, UserInfo] = {}

        # Locations: {(city, neighborhood): LocationInfo}, allows geographic filtering
        self.locations: Dict[Tuple[str, str], LocationInfo] = {}

        # Constraints reminder:
        # - Each review must be associated with an existing business and user
        # - A user cannot submit more than one review per business
        # - Business names and locations must be validated to prevent duplicates
        # - Reviews are displayed in chronological or relevance-ordered fashion by default
        # - Supports text-based and location-based search queries

            lon_min (float): Minimum longitude (inclusive).

            }
            or

                "success": False,
                "error": str  # Description of error, e.g., invalid bounds
            }

        Constraints:
            - The coordinate bounds must be valid (min <= max for both lat and lon).
            - Only businesses with valid coordinates are considered.
        """
        # Validate coordinate bounds
        if lat_min > lat_max:
            return {"success": False, "error": "Invalid latitude bounds: lat_min > lat_max"}
        if lon_min > lon_max:
            return {"success": False, "error": "Invalid longitude bounds: lon_min > lon_max"}

        result = []
        for business in self.businesses.values():
            lat = business["latitude"]
            lon = business["longitude"]
            if lat_min <= lat <= lat_max and lon_min <= lon <= lon_max:
                result.append(business)

        return {"success": True, "data": result}"}, "get_top_reviews_by_helpful_count": {"signature": {"parameters": [{"name": "business_id", "type": "str", "default": null, "kind": "positional-or-keyword"}], "return": "dict"}, "doc": "Retrieve the most helpful reviews for a given business, sorted by helpful_count in descending order.

        self,
        user_id: str,
        business_id: str,
        rating: float,
        text: str,
        timestamp: str
    ) -> dict:
        """
        Submit a new review for a business by a user, if one does not already exist.

        Args:
            user_id (str): The ID of the user submitting the review.
            business_id (str): The ID of the business being reviewed.
            rating (float): The rating given to the business (e.g., 1.0 to 5.0).
            text (str): The textual content of the review.
            timestamp (str): The time of submission in ISO or Unix timestamp format.

        Returns:
            dict: {
                "success": True,
                "message": "Review submitted successfully"
            }
            or
            {
                "success": False,
                "error": str  # Description of the error (e.g., business not found, duplicate review)
            }

        Constraints:
            - The business and user must exist.
            - A user cannot submit more than one review per business.
            - The review is added with initial helpful_count = 0.
            - The user's review_count is incremented by 1 upon successful submission.
        """
        # Check if business exists
        if business_id not in self.businesses:
            return { "success": False, "error": "Business does not exist" }

        # Check if user exists
        if user_id not in self.users:
            return { "success": False, "error": "User does not exist" }

        # Check if user already reviewed this business
        for review in self.reviews.values():
            if review["user_id"] == user_id and review["business_id"] == business_id:
                return { "success": False, "error": "User has already reviewed this business" }

        # Generate unique review_id (simple approach: use length of current reviews)
        review_id = f"review_{len(self.reviews)}"

        # Create new review
        new_review: ReviewInfo = {
            "review_id": review_id,
            "business_id": business_id,
            "user_id": user_id,
            "rating": rating,
            "text": text,
            "timestamp": timestamp,
            "helpful_count": 0
        }

        # Add review to system
        self.reviews[review_id] = new_review

        # Increment user's review count
        self.users[user_id]["review_count"] += 1

        return { "success": True, "message": "Review submitted successfully" }"}, "add_business": {"signature": {"parameters": [{"name": "business_info", "type": "BusinessInfo", "default": null, "kind": "positional-or-keyword"}], "return": "dict"}, "doc": "Register a new business listing after validating for duplicates.

        """
        Register a new business listing after validating for duplicates.

        Args:
            business_info (BusinessInfo): Dictionary containing business details including:
                - business_id: str
                - name: str
                - address: str
                - city: str
                - latitude: float (must be between -90 and 90)
                - longitude: float (must be between -180 and 180)
                - category: str
                - phone: str
                - website: str

        Returns:
            dict: {
                "success": bool,
                "message": str  # On success
            }
            or
            {
                "success": False,
                "error": str  # Reason for failure
            }

        Constraints:
            - The business_id must be unique.
            - No other business with the same name, address, and city can exist.
            - Latitude must be in [-90, 90], longitude in [-180, 180].
            - All fields are required.
        """
        required_fields = [
            "business_id", "name", "address", "city", "latitude", "longitude",
            "category", "phone", "website"
        ]
        for field in required_fields:
            if field not in business_info:
                return {"success": False, "error": f"Missing required field: {field}"}

        business_id = business_info["business_id"]
        name = business_info["name"]
        address = business_info["address"]
        city = business_info["city"]
        latitude = business_info["latitude"]
        longitude = business_info["longitude"]

        # Validate coordinates
        if not (-90 <= latitude <= 90):
            return {"success": False, "error": "Latitude must be between -90 and 90"}
        if not (-180 <= longitude <= 180):
            return {"success": False, "error": "Longitude must be between -180 and 180"}

        # Check for duplicate business_id
        if business_id in self.businesses:
            return {"success": False, "error": "A business with this ID already exists"}

        # Check for duplicate name, address, and city
        for existing in self.businesses.values():
            if (
                existing["name"].lower() == name.lower()
                and existing["address"].lower() == address.lower()
                and existing["city"].lower() == city.lower()
            ):
                return {"success": False, "error": "A business with the same name, address, and city already exists"}

        # Add the business
        self.businesses[business_id] = business_info

        return {"success": True, "message": "Business added successfully"}"}, "update_business_details": {"signature": {"parameters": [{"name": "business_id", "type": "str", "default": null, "kind": "positional-or-keyword"}, {"name": "updates", "type": "dict", "default": null, "kind": "positional-or-keyword"}], "return": "dict"}, "doc": "Modify existing business information such as phone, website, address, etc.

            }

        Constraints:
            - The business must exist.
            - Only valid business fields (excluding business_id) can be updated.
            - Business names and locations should remain valid (no duplicate entries enforced via this method).
        """
        if business_id not in self.businesses:
            return { "success": False, "error": "Business not found" }

        valid_fields = {
            'name', 'address', 'city', 'latitude', 'longitude',
            'category', 'phone', 'website'
        }

        business = self.businesses[business_id]

        # Check for invalid fields in updates
        invalid_fields = set(updates.keys()) - valid_fields
        if invalid_fields:
            return {
                "success": False,
                "error": f"Invalid fields cannot be updated: {', '.join(invalid_fields)}"
            }

        # Apply valid updates
        for key, value in updates.items():
            if key in valid_fields:
                business[key] = value  # Update the field

        return { "success": True, "message": "Business details updated successfully." }"}, "delete_review": {"signature": {"parameters": [{"name": "review_id", "type": "str", "default": null, "kind": "positional-or-keyword"}], "return": "dict"}, "doc": "Remove a user's review from the system by review ID.

        """
        Remove a user's review from the system by review ID.

        Args:
            review_id (str): The unique identifier of the review to delete.

        Returns:
            dict: {
                "success": True,
                "message": "Review deleted successfully"
            }
            or
            {
                "success": False,
                "error": "Review not found"
            }

        Constraints:
            - The review must exist.
            - The associated user must exist (if not, review is still deleted but user is not updated).
            - The user's review_count is decremented by 1 (minimum 0).
        """
        if review_id not in self.reviews:
            return {"success": False, "error": "Review not found"}

        review = self.reviews[review_id]
        user_id = review["user_id"]

        # Delete the review
        del self.reviews[review_id]

        # Update user's review_count if user exists
        if user_id in self.users:
            self.users[user_id]["review_count"] = max(0, self.users[user_id]["review_count"] - 1)

        return {"success": True, "message": "Review deleted successfully"}"}, "increment_helpful_count": {"signature": {"parameters": [{"name": "review_id", "type": "str", "default": null, "kind": "positional-or-keyword"}], "return": "dict"}, "doc": "Increment the helpful_count of a specified review by 1.

        """
        Add multiple businesses to the platform with duplicate validation based on name, address, and city.
    
        Args:
            businesses (List[BusinessInfo]): A list of business dictionaries to import.
                Each must include: business_id, name, address, city, latitude, longitude, category, phone, website.
    
        Returns:
            dict: {
                "success": bool,
                "message": str  # Describes how many were imported and how many were skipped
            }
            In case of input error:
            {
                "success": False,
                "error": str
            }

        Constraints:
            - Each business must have a unique combination of name, address, and city to avoid duplicates.
            - Business data must include all required fields.
        """
        if not isinstance(businesses, list):
            return {"success": False, "error": "Input must be a list of businesses."}

        imported_count = 0
        skipped_count = 0

        for business in businesses:
            # Validate required fields
            required_keys = {
                "business_id", "name", "address", "city", "latitude", "longitude", "category", "phone", "website"
            }
            if not isinstance(business, dict) or not all(k in business for k in required_keys):
                skipped_count += 1
                continue  # Skip invalid entry

            bid = business["business_id"]
            name = business["name"]
            address = business["address"]
            city = business["city"]

            # Check for duplicates: same name, address, and city
            is_duplicate = False
            for existing in self.businesses.values():
                if (
                    existing["name"] == name
                    and existing["address"] == address
                    and existing["city"] == city
                ):
                    is_duplicate = True
                    break

            if is_duplicate:
                skipped_count += 1
            else:
                self.businesses[bid] = BusinessInfo(
                    business_id=bid,
                    name=name,
                    address=address,
                    city=city,
                    latitude=business["latitude"],
                    longitude=business["longitude"],
                    category=business["category"],
                    phone=business["phone"],
                    website=business["website"]

from datetime import date

class LeagueInfo(TypedDict):
    league_id: str
    name: str
    country: str
    season_start_date: str  # ISO format date string, e.g., "2024-08-01"
    season_end_date: str
    status: str  # "upcoming", "active", "completed"

class TeamInfo(TypedDict):
    team_id: str
    name: str
    city: str
    league_id: str
    roster: List[str]  # List of player names or IDs

class FixtureInfo(TypedDict):
    match_id: str
    league_id: str
    home_team_id: str
    away_team_id: str
    venue: str  # venue_id
    match_date: str  # ISO format timestamp or date-time
    status: str  # "scheduled", "completed", etc.

class VenueInfo(TypedDict):
    venue_id: str
    name: str
    city: str
    capacity: int
    home_team_id: str

        self,
        league_id: str,
        name: str,
        country: str,
        season_start_date: str,
        season_end_date: str
    ) -> dict:
        """
        Add a new league to the system with defined start and end dates.
        The status is set automatically:
        - "upcoming" if season_start_date is in the future.
        - "active" if current date is within the season.
        - "completed" if season_end_date is in the past.

        Args:
            league_id (str): Unique identifier for the league.
            name (str): Name of the league.
            country (str): Country where the league is organized.
            season_start_date (str): Start date in ISO format (e.g., "2024-08-01").
            season_end_date (str): End date in ISO format.

        Returns:
            dict: { "success": True, "message": "League added successfully." }
                  or { "success": False, "error": "reason" }

        Constraints:
            - league_id must be unique.
            - season_start_date must be <= season_end_date.
            - status is determined by current date relative to season dates.
        """
        # Check if league_id already exists
        if league_id in self.leagues:
            return { "success": False, "error": f"League with id '{league_id}' already exists." }

        # Validate date format and logical order
        try:
            start = datetime.fromisoformat(season_start_date)
            end = datetime.fromisoformat(season_end_date)
        except ValueError as e:
            return { "success": False, "error": f"Invalid date format: {str(e)}" }

        if start > end:
            return { "success": False, "error": "Season start date must be before or equal to end date." }

        # Determine status based on current date
        now = datetime.now()
        if start > now:
            status = "upcoming"
        elif end < now:
            status = "completed"
        else:
            status = "active"

        # Create new league entry
        self.leagues[league_id] = LeagueInfo(
            league_id=league_id,
            name=name,
            country=country,
            season_start_date=season_start_date,
            season_end_date=season_end_date,
            status=status
        )

        return { "success": True, "message": "League added successfully." }"}, "update_league_status": {"signature": {"parameters": [{"name": "league_id", "type": "str", "default": null, "kind": "positional-or-keyword"}], "return": "dict"}, "doc": "Automatically update the status of a league based on current date relative to its season dates.

        """
        Automatically update the status of a league based on current date relative to its season dates.
    
        Args:
            league_id (str): The ID of the league to update.

        Returns:
            dict: {
                "success": bool,
                "message": str  # Describes the new status or failure reason
            }

        Constraints:
            - Status is determined by comparing the current date with season_start_date and season_end_date.
            - If season_start_date > today: status = "upcoming"
            - If season_start_date <= today <= season_end_date: status = "active"
            - If today > season_end_date: status = "completed"
        """
        if league_id not in self.leagues:
            return { "success": False, "error": "League not found" }

        league = self.leagues[league_id]
        start_date = league["season_start_date"]
        end_date = league["season_end_date"]

        # Get current date (in simulation, use today's date in ISO format)
        today = datetime.today().strftime('%Y-%m-%d')

        # Determine new status
        if today < start_date:
            new_status = "upcoming"
        elif start_date <= today <= end_date:
            new_status = "active"
        else:  # today > end_date
            new_status = "completed"

        # Update the league status
        league["status"] = new_status

        return {
            "success": True,
            "message": f"League status updated to {new_status}"
        }"}, "add_team": {"signature": {"parameters": [{"name": "team_id", "type": "str", "default": null, "kind": "positional-or-keyword"}, {"name": "name", "type": "str", "default": null, "kind": "positional-or-keyword"}, {"name": "city", "type": "str", "default": null, "kind": "positional-or-keyword"}, {"name": "league_id", "type": "str", "default": null, "kind": "positional-or-keyword"}, {"name": "roster", "type": "List[str]", "default": null, "kind": "positional-or-keyword"}], "return": "dict"}, "doc": "Register a new team and assign it to a league, ensuring it belongs to only one league per season.

        # Check if fixture exists
        if match_id not in self.fixtures:
            return {"success": False, "error": "Fixture not found"}

        fixture = self.fixtures[match_id]

        current_date = fixture["match_date"]
        current_venue = fixture["venue"]

        # Use new values or fallback to current ones
        final_date = new_match_date if new_match_date is not None else current_date
        final_venue = new_venue if new_venue is not None else current_venue

        # Validate league exists
        if league_id not in self.leagues:
            return {"success": False, "error": "League for the fixture not found"}

        league = self.leagues[league_id]

        if home_team_id == away_team_id:

        # Check both teams belong to the same league
        if (

    dict: {
        "success": True,

    }

    season_start_date and season_end_date. It does not rely solely on the stored 'status'
    field to ensure up-to-date results.

Constraints:
    - A league is active if: season_start_date <= today <= season_end_date.

env_109_sft.environment_introduction: A social media content platform maintains user profiles, generated content (such as images, videos, and reels), timestamps, and engagement data in a structured, stateful environment. It supports operations like content upload, retrieval by user or type, and chronological sorting. The system enables users to consume and interact with multimedia content in a dynamic feed-based interface.

state_space_definition.attributes: _id, username, bio, profile_image, follower_count, following_count, account_typ
state_space_definition.description: Represents a platform user. The user_id is a key identifier for retrieving associated content.

state_space_definition.attributes: content_id, user_id, content_type, media_url, caption, timestamp, like_count, comment_count, share_count, view_coun
state_space_definition.description: Represents a piece of user-generated media. The content_type distinguishes between images, videos, reels, etc., and timestamp enables chronological sorting.

state_space_definition.attributes: feed_id, user_id, content_list, refresh_timestamp, filter_criteria
state_space_definition.description: Represents a dynamically generated feed of content, potentially filtered or sorted for display.

constraints_rules: Only publicly posted content or content from followed users (depending on privacy settings) can be retrieved.
Content must be sorted in descending order by timestamp to show the latest first.
Each content item must be associated with a valid user_id.
The content_type attribute must be one of the supported types (e.g., "image", "video", "reel").
Retrieval operations must support pagination or limits (e.g., "latest 5") for performance and UX.

operation_list.operation_description: Retrieve user profile information using their unique user ID.
Retrieve user info by username (for human-readable lookup).
Retrieve all content posted by a specific user, regardless of type.
Retrieve content from a user filtered by content_type (e.g., "reel").
Retrieve the most recent content items from a user, sorted by timestamp in descending order.
Retrieve a paginated list of latest content (e.g., latest 5) from a user, sorted and limited.
Retrieve content filtered by type and limited in number (e.g., latest 5 reels).
Retrieve full details of a specific content item by content_id.
Retrieve or generate a personalized feed for a user based on their following and preferences.
Determine if a piece of content is publicly visible or accessible based on privacy and follow status.
Retrieve engagement metrics (likes, comments, shares, views) for a content item.
Add new user-generated content to the system with valid user_id and supported content_type.
Update a user's content feed by reapplying filter criteria and sorting, updating the refresh_timestamp.
Modify the caption of an existing content item.
Remove a content item from the platform (requires ownership verification).
Increment the like_count of a content item (simulates user engagement).
Increment the share_count and optionally log the sharing action.
Modify the filter settings (e.g., content type, source) used to generate a user's feed.
Create or regenerate a ContentFeed with specific filters (e.g., "reels from following").

from typing import Dict, List, TypedDict
import time
from typing import Any, List, Dict as TypedDict



class UserInfo(TypedDict):
    _id: str
    username: str
    bio: str
    profile_image: str
    follower_count: int
    following_count: int
    account_type: str  # corrected from 'account_typ'

class ContentInfo(TypedDict):
    content_id: str
    user_id: str
    content_type: str  # one of: "image", "video", "reel"
    media_url: str
    caption: str
    timestamp: float  # Unix timestamp or ISO format as float
    like_count: int
    comment_count: int
    share_count: int
    view_count: int  # corrected from 'view_coun'

class ContentFeedInfo(TypedDict):
    feed_id: str
    user_id: str
    content_list: List[str]  # list of content_id strings
    refresh_timestamp: float
    filter_criteria: dict  # flexible filtering params (e.g., {"type": "reel", "source": "following"})

class SocialMediaContentPlatform:
    def __init__(self):
        """
        A social media content platform (Instagram-like) managing users, content, and dynamic feeds.
        """

        # Users: {_id: UserInfo}
        self.users: Dict[str, UserInfo] = {}

        # Content: {content_id: ContentInfo}
        self.content: Dict[str, ContentInfo] = {}

        # ContentFeeds: {feed_id: ContentFeedInfo}
        self.feeds: Dict[str, ContentFeedInfo] = {}

        # Supported content types
        self.supported_content_types: List[str] = ["image", "video", "reel"]

        # - Each content item must be associated with a valid user_id
        # - content_type must be one of: "image", "video", "reel"
        # - Retrieval operations must support pagination (e.g., limit=5)

            - Content is sorted in descending order by timestamp (latest first).
            - Only content with supported types ("image", "video", "reel") is included.
            - Feed limits results to latest 20 items (pagination).

        if user_id not in self.users:
            return {"success": False, "error": "User not found"}

        # Filter content: only valid user_id and supported content types
        valid_content = []
        for content_info in self.content.values():
            if (
                content_info["user_id"] in self.users
                and content_info["content_type"] in self.supported_content_types
            ):
                valid_content.append(content_info)

        # Sort by timestamp descending (latest first)
        sorted_content = sorted(valid_content, key=lambda x: x["timestamp"], reverse=True)

        # Apply pagination: get latest 20
        latest_content_ids = [c["content_id"] for c in sorted_content[:20]]

        # Use time module directly to get current timestamp
        current_timestamp = time.time()

        # Create feed representation
        feed = {

            }

        """
        Determine if a piece of content is visible to the requester based on the owner's privacy settings
        and whether the requester follows the owner.

        Args:
            content_id (str): The ID of the content to check visibility for.
            requester_user_id (str): The ID of the user attempting to view the content.

        Returns:
            dict: {
                "success": bool,
                "data": {"visible": bool}  # If successful, whether the content is visible
            }
            or
            {
                "success": False,
                "error": str  # Reason for failure (e.g., content not found)
            }

        Constraints:
            - If the content owner's account is "public", the content is visible to all.
            - If the account is "private", only followers can see the content.
            - The requester must be a valid user, and the content must exist.
            - A mapping `self.followers` (user_id -> set of follower user_ids) is assumed to exist.

        Note:
            This method assumes `self.followers: Dict[str, set]` is maintained by the system.
            If not, visibility for private accounts cannot be determined.
        """
        # Check if content exists
        if content_id not in self.content:
            return { "success": False, "error": "Content not found" }

        content = self.content[content_id]
        owner_id = content["user_id"]

        # Check if owner exists
        if owner_id not in self.users:
            return { "success": False, "error": "Content owner not found" }

        # Check if requester exists
        if requester_user_id not in self.users:
            return { "success": False, "error": "Requester user not found" }

        owner = self.users[owner_id]
        account_type = owner.get("account_type", "public").lower()

        # Public account: visible to everyone
        if account_type == "public":
            return { "success": True, "data": { "visible": True } }

        # Private account: only visible to followers
        if account_type == "private":
            # Assume self.followers exists and maps user_id -> set of follower user_ids
            if not hasattr(self, "followers"):
                return { "success": False, "error": "Follow relationship tracking is not available" }

            followers = self.followers.get(owner_id, set())
            is_follower = requester_user_id in followers
            return { "success": True, "data": { "visible": is_follower } }

        # Unknown account type
        return { "success": False, "error": f"Unknown account type: {account_type}" }"}, "get_content_statistics": {"signature": {"parameters": [{"name": "content_id", "type": "str", "default": null, "kind": "positional-or-keyword"}], "return": "dict"}, "doc": "Retrieve engagement metrics (likes, comments, shares, views) for a specific content item.

        self,
        content_id: str,

        media_url: str,
        caption: str,
        timestamp: float,
        like_count: int = 0,
        comment_count: int = 0,
        share_count: int = 0,
        view_count: int = 0
    ) -> dict:
        """
        Add new user-generated content to the system.

        Args:
            content_id (str): Unique identifier for the content.

            content_type (str): Type of content. Must be one of: "image", "video", "reel".

        Returns:

        if content_id in self.content:

        if user_id not in self.users:

        if content_type not in self.supported_content_types:

        # Create new content entry
